elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph warrants only that the Hosting and Support Services will "conform in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement" for 30 days; no professional-and-workmanlike (or industry-standard) warranty is added. Section 11's "same degree of care, skill and prudence customarily exercised by it for its own operations" is a self-referential performance covenant, not a warranty of professional and workmanlike performance.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "the Interface and all related software will conform in all material respects to its documentation".

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Inserted period is "ninety (90) days following delivery" for software, not 12 months.
Inserted services period is "thirty (30) days following performance", not 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "at TrueLink's option, repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or re-performance of the non-conforming Services".
Inserted: "or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming software or Services".

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in Section 9 as rendered or elsewhere in the cited operative language.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code / virus warranty is present in the rendered language; Section 9 covers only Year 2000 date handling plus the new conformance warranty.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "(i) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, the Interface and all related software will conform in all material respects to its documentation" — 90 days satisfies the "at least 90 days" floor notwithstanding the failing period regex, which does not reflect the operative text.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "(ii) for a period of thirty (30) days following performance, the Hosting Services and Support Services will conform in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement"; both service categories are defined/used in the Agreement.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted remedy sentence expressly provides "repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or re-performance of the non-conforming Services", at Vendor's option as contemplated by the model language.
Inserted remedy sentence provides "a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming software or Services".

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: the single inserted paragraph supplies a 90-day software conformance warranty, a 30-day services conformance warranty, and a repair/replacement-or-refund remedy, all in operative language rather than in the comment.

The deterministic check "warranty period ≥ 90 days or expressed in months/years" reports not ok, but substantive inspection of the rendered text shows "a period of ninety (90) days following delivery" for software; the check appears to be misfiring on the 30-day services tail, and the fallback floor is met on the operative wording.

Preferred level is not reached: no professional-and-workmanlike warranty, software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, services period is 30 days rather than 90 days, and there is no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty. The comment correctly and non-lecturing-ly discloses this and names the preferred position.

Minimal: the edit adds exactly the four fallback elements in one sentence pair, with no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no notice/claim procedure, and no added damages categories; it leaves the favourable Year 2000 warranty and the express-warranty carve-out in the disclaimer untouched rather than restating them.

Preserves intent: the disclaimer's "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT" opener already preserves the new express warranty, so no contradictory retained sentence arises; Section 11's standard of care coexists with the new warranty; and all terms used (Interface, Hosting Services, Support Services, Client, TrueLink) are defined in the Agreement with no dangling cross-references.
